recent_story_cards.conflict: The narrator knows someone is taking their food but has no proof until the thief exposes herself by complaining about the meal.
recent_story_cards.payoff: You filed a complaint about food you stole.
recent_story_cards.premise: A coworker secretly steals the narrator's homemade lunches for a week, then reports the narrator to HR after taking a naturally extra-spicy meal.
recent_story_cards.title: She Stole My Lunch, Then Reported Me to HR
recent_story_cards.twist: The coworker identifies herself as the lunch thief by filing an HR complaint about food that was never hers.

recent_story_cards.conflict: The narrator becomes convinced a hidden jewelry purchase means a proposal is coming, while her boyfriend acts increasingly secretive and keeps disappearing to make mysterious calls.
recent_story_cards.payoff: I should have told you the truth years ago.
recent_story_cards.premise: A woman thinks her boyfriend is secretly planning to propose after finding a hidden jewelry receipt, but discovers he bought an expensive bracelet for his mother to replace one he accidentally lost years ago.
recent_story_cards.title: I Thought He Was About to Propose
recent_story_cards.twist: The jewelry was never an engagement ring; he was replacing his mother's sentimental bracelet after finally admitting he lost the original years earlier.

recent_story_cards.conflict: The narrator and another roommate trust the bill-paying roommate's claim that a separate maintenance fee is required, until the landlord confirms the fee does not exist and reveals that the actual rent has also been paid late.
recent_story_cards.payoff: You invented a fee and forgot to pay the real rent.
recent_story_cards.premise: A woman discovers that the roommate who handles the apartment bills has been collecting a fake monthly maintenance fee from everyone while repeatedly paying the real rent late.
recent_story_cards.title: My Roommate Invented a Fake Rent Fee
recent_story_cards.twist: The roommate posing as the responsible household money manager has been pocketing the invented fee and is exposed when the landlord arrives over late rent despite everyone else paying her early.

recent_story_cards.conflict: The narrator's manager takes sole credit for her work and sidelines her during the client meeting, assuming he can present the deck without understanding the research behind it.
recent_story_cards.payoff: You put your name on my work. You should have learned how it worked.
recent_story_cards.premise: A woman spends weeks building a client presentation, only for her manager to remove her name and present it as his own, until the client asks about a hidden appendix slide he never bothered to read.
recent_story_cards.title: My Manager Stole My Presentation—Then the Client Opened the Last Slide
recent_story_cards.twist: The manager is exposed by a client question about an appendix slide that credits the narrator by name and contains a technical decision only she can explain.

recent_story_cards.conflict: The narrator is threatened with condo penalties over late-night barking even though she has no pet, while the neighbor across the hall keeps presenting suspiciously precise recordings as proof.
recent_story_cards.payoff: You were reporting your own recording.
recent_story_cards.premise: A woman receives repeated condo noise complaints about a dog she does not own, then discovers her neighbor has been playing barking sounds outside her door to manufacture evidence and pressure her to move.
recent_story_cards.title: She Reported My Dog. I Don't Own One.
recent_story_cards.twist: Hallway camera footage reveals the complaining neighbor secretly placing a Bluetooth speaker near the narrator's door and playing barking audio so the complaints would appear legitimate.

recent_story_cards.conflict: Her boyfriend turns a reasonable question about a repeated Thursday-night location into an argument about trust and privacy, convincing friends she is obsessively tracking him while he continues visiting the restaurant in secret.
recent_story_cards.payoff: You turned off your location, but you kept using my rewards account.
recent_story_cards.premise: A woman questions why her boyfriend appears at the same restaurant every Thursday, gets accused of being controlling when he disables location sharing, then discovers he has been secretly dating someone else because he kept using her restaurant rewards account on every visit.
recent_story_cards.title: He Turned Off His Location. He Forgot My Rewards Account.
recent_story_cards.twist: After he disables location sharing, the restaurant contacts her rewards account about repeated Thursday visits, revealing that he kept entering her phone number for points while taking another woman there.

recent_story_cards.conflict: The narrator sees repeated unfamiliar smart-lock entries while away, but her best friend insists she is imagining a technical problem and says nobody else has been inside the apartment.
recent_story_cards.payoff: You weren't dog-sitting. You were running an Airbnb out of my apartment.
recent_story_cards.premise: A woman leaves her best friend one key to feed her dog during a four-day trip, then discovers the friend has secretly listed her apartment as a short-term rental while pretending the unexpected smart-lock alerts are glitches.
recent_story_cards.title: My Best Friend Rented Out My Apartment While I Was Away
recent_story_cards.twist: A confused rental guest calls the narrator using the emergency contact card on the fridge, proving the best friend rented out the apartment and had been entering only to reset it between guests.

recent_story_cards.conflict: The narrator keeps receiving warnings for messes found after meetings booked under her name, while a coworker insists she must be forgetting to clean up and management begins treating her as irresponsible.
recent_story_cards.payoff: You weren't hiding behind the meeting room. You were hiding behind my name.
recent_story_cards.premise: A woman is repeatedly blamed for leaving the office meeting room filthy after late client calls, until the cleaner's timestamped photos reveal her coworker has been using her calendar bookings to hide his own after-hours side business.
recent_story_cards.title: He Used My Meeting Room Booking as His Alibi
recent_story_cards.twist: The cleaner's timestamped photos show the coworker entering after the narrator leaves and using her still-active room reservations to conduct paid consulting calls he is forbidden to run from the office.

recent_story_cards.conflict: The narrator starts questioning whether she is missing notifications or overreacting, while the organizer publicly acts concerned, repeatedly re-adds her to an inactive group, and tells everyone the messaging app is unreliable.
recent_story_cards.payoff: The app wasn't excluding me. You were.
recent_story_cards.premise: A woman keeps getting left out of her friend group's dinners and weekend plans because the organizer claims the group chat is glitching, until a newly added friend shows her screenshots proving the organizer has been deliberately making a second chat without her.
recent_story_cards.title: My Friends Said the Group Chat Was Glitching
recent_story_cards.twist: A new member accidentally sends the narrator screenshots from the active group, revealing months of planning, jokes about keeping her out, and the organizer's repeated instructions to use the other chat whenever the narrator was available.

recent_story_cards.conflict: The bride is blamed for being controlling when she questions why her parents and elderly relatives were moved, while her future mother-in-law repeatedly claims the venue software automatically rearranged the tables.
recent_story_cards.payoff: The venue didn't move my family. You did.
recent_story_cards.premise: A bride discovers that her future mother-in-law secretly rewrote the wedding seating chart to push the bride's parents to the back of the room and give the best tables to her own friends, while insisting the venue made the changes.
recent_story_cards.title: She Rewrote My Wedding Seating Chart
recent_story_cards.twist: At the final venue meeting, the coordinator opens the seating-plan revision history and every disputed change is traced to the future mother-in-law's guest login, including notes labeling the bride's relatives as lower priority.

recent_story_cards.conflict: The customer is told the salon's computer records are definitive and is threatened with losing booking privileges, even though she has receipts, photos, and card charges proving she was physically there for the disputed appointments.
recent_story_cards.payoff: I wasn't a no-show. You sold my appointment twice.
recent_story_cards.premise: A salon customer is charged repeated no-show fees for appointments she actually attended, then discovers the receptionist has been marking completed visits as missed so she can resell popular time slots for cash tips.
recent_story_cards.title: The Salon Charged Me for an Appointment I Attended
recent_story_cards.twist: When the owner compares payment timestamps with booking records, she discovers the receptionist checked the narrator out under walk-in transactions, marked the original reservations as no-shows, and quietly reassigned those same slots to customers willing to pay extra.

recent_story_cards.conflict: The expecting mother notices gifts vanishing after the shower while her mother-in-law insists she is simply overwhelmed and has forgotten what people gave.
recent_story_cards.payoff: Those gifts weren't duplicates. You just decided you had the right to return them.
recent_story_cards.premise: A grandmother-to-be offers to organize baby shower gifts, then secretly returns several expensive presents for store credit on her own account because she thinks the parents received too much.
recent_story_cards.title: She Returned My Baby Shower Gifts for Credit
recent_story_cards.twist: At the baby store, an employee recognizes the mother-in-law and thanks her for the large batch of returns she made using the shower gift receipts.
